evidence: the-agent-run-purges-it: baseline :21-22 declare both IPv6 chains with purge => true and policy => drop, so an agent run must delete hand-added rules from INPUT and FORWARD and keep the managed lo rule; the effect counts 0 planted rules, 1 lo rule and both -P DROP lines after the node agent run (rc 2, 2 changed = the two purged rules)

a-desktop-login-works-under-the-drop-policy: baseline :5-7 say desktop session components may use ::1 during login and :13-19 accept all IPv6 on lo for that; on the kubuntu node with the class applied, a fresh user's SDDM autologin brings up plasmashell within 180 s while INPUT is still DROP. The probe tests that login works under the policy; it does not time the login against a version without the lo rule, so it shows no hang rather than no delay

the-forward-policy-counted-the-routed-packets: baseline :21 sets the IPv6 FORWARD policy to drop with no rules, so packets the peer routes through the node can only end at the policy; the effect reads the FORWARD policy-DROP packet counter (>= 5 after the peer's 5 routed pings) and fails on the clean node, where the policy is ACCEPT

purpose covered: The purpose (IPv6 INPUT/FORWARD dropped by default, IPv6 loopback open on lo for desktop logins, no unmanaged IPv6 rules) matches the baseline header comment (:1-7) and code (:13-22: one lo accept rule, two firewallchains with purge and policy drop). The checks test what the class does: exact policies and the lo rule; ping and TCP to ::1 working on the node; a peer on the link dropped over IPv6 (ICMPv6 and SSH) but still reaching SSH over IPv4; packets routed through the node dropped by the FORWARD policy (counter); a hand-planted rule in each chain purged by the next agent run; and a real Plasma/SDDM login on the kubuntu variant under the DROP policy. The outcomes table has no uncovered rows and maps every outcome to a check that probes it. My run: all 8 base negative controls failed on the clean node and passed after apply; the desktop variant control failed clean and passed applied (ALL_PASS). What is left out: the claim that dropping ::1 causes login delays is not measured, because no run without the lo rule is timed. That would test the comment, not the class, which keeps ::1 open; the purpose outcome (login works under the policy) is tested.
